title: Do Not Commit to Anyone
coreMove: Keep alignment valuable by delaying capture until the price of commitment is visible
sourcePressure: Chapter 20 is supported here by the frozen title and grouped secondary summaries: commitment can reduce leverage when you tie yourself too quickly to one side, while noncommitment can preserve independence because multiple sides still want your alignment. The mechanism should stay narrow. The chapter is about optionality, capture risk, and timing, not about condemning all loyalty or all cooperation. Keep it grounded in side-taking cost, leverage retention, and the limit that empty drift is not the same as strategic independence. Avoid invented court, battlefield, or palace anecdotes and avoid turning the law into generic anti-relationship advice. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
